name: Japan
tagline: Real English-taught degrees — but the biggest door just closed
summary: Japan built a small, deliberate set of fully English-taught bachelor's degrees over the last fifteen years, and an IB Diploma is the qualification most of them were designed around. The awkward news for anyone starting in 2027 is that the most famous of them, the University of Tokyo's PEAK, has stopped recruiting: September 2026 was its final intake. What remains is still substantial — Waseda's six English-based schools, Keio, Sophia, ICU, Tohoku, Kyoto's iUP, APU and Akita — but you are choosing from roughly forty programmes nationally, not four hundred. The deeper thing to understand is the calendar. Japanese universities run two separate intakes, April and September, and applications for a September 2027 start typically open in autumn 2026 and close in January or February 2027, before your IB results exist. Everything hinges on predicted grades.
whyConsider: Waseda's application window for September entry ran 8 January to 10 February in the most recent cycle — late enough that predicted grades are settled, which is unusually friendly compared with Japan's older October deadlines.

Kyoto's iUP takes you with no Japanese at all: a six-month preparatory course, then four years of undergraduate study, 4.5 years in total, with fee waivers and monthly scholarships for eligible students.
National-university tuition in Japan is low by global standards, and private universities are far cheaper than their US or UK equivalents — though we could not verify the 2027 figures.
MEXT (Monbukagakusho) scholarships exist specifically for undergraduate degree students and are applied for through the Japanese embassy in Copenhagen, not through the university.
Several programmes — ICU, Akita International University, APU — are built entirely around a bilingual liberal-arts model that maps naturally onto the IB's breadth.
watchOuts: The University of Tokyo's PEAK has ended. Its own site states that the September 2026 intake was the final student recruitment. Anyone starting in 2027 cannot apply to it, and no replacement has been announced.
UTokyo's other English route, the Global Science Course, is a third-year transfer programme requiring at least two years of undergraduate study outside Japan. It is not an entry point from gymnasium.

Deadlines are the single biggest trap. Many Japanese programmes close applications in the autumn or early winter for the following September, and some close in the summer for an April start. You must build a spreadsheet of individual deadlines in September 2026.
Two intakes means two calendars. April 2027 entry would mean applying in mid-2026, before your final IB year is finished — realistically impossible. Target September/October 2027.

We could not verify a single 2027 tuition figure from an official page during this research. Every cost below is left blank here rather than guessed at, and must be confirmed directly with each university before you rely on it.
Denmark's SU does not follow you to Japan on the same terms as an EU/EEA country. Check with su.dk early; a full degree outside the EU/EEA has separate rules.
Japanese universities generally want documents apostilled and sometimes notarised, and a Certificate of Eligibility must be obtained before the student visa. Start three months before travel.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Not verified from an official source in this research. Japanese English-taught programmes generally treat the full IB Diploma as satisfying the 12-year education requirement under Japan's School Education Act, and then apply their own competitive standard on top. Individual programmes set their own HL expectations.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. Each university reads IB points directly.
notes: The IB Diploma is one of the qualifications Japan's English-taught programmes were explicitly designed to receive, alongside A-levels, the US high school diploma plus SAT/ACT, and the Abitur.
Many programmes ask for predicted grades plus the final diploma as a condition of enrolment, so an IB student is not disadvantaged by finishing in May.
Some programmes also want SAT/ACT or a national university entrance examination for international students (EJU). Check each one — the requirements are not uniform.
Minimum point scores were not published on any page we could read. Treat anything quoted elsewhere as unverified.

portal.name: No central portal — apply direct to each university

deadlines.label: Waseda English-based undergraduate programmes (six schools)
deadlines.year: 2026 cycle for September 2026 entry; 2027 dates expected to follow the same pattern but were not published at the time of research
deadlines.notes: One application window covering the School of Political Science and Economics, School of Social Sciences, SILS, School of Culture Media and Society, and the two Science and Engineering schools.

deadlines.label: Kyoto University iUP, October 2027 enrolment
deadlines.notes: Application guidelines for October 2027 enrolment were published on 1 July 2026. The exact deadline was not stated on the page we read — download the guidelines from the iUP site.

deadlines.label: University of Tokyo PEAK
deadlines.notes: PEAK is no longer recruiting. Do not include it in a 2027 shortlist.

deadlines.label: MEXT scholarship, embassy recommendation route
deadlines.notes: Applications normally open through the Japanese embassy in the spring of the year before enrolment. Deadline not verified — contact the Embassy of Japan in Denmark in early 2026.

steps: In September 2026, build a spreadsheet of every English-taught programme you are interested in, with its intake month and its own deadline. There is no central portal and no shared calendar.
Decide April or September. For an IB student finishing in May 2027, September or October 2027 is the only realistic entry.
Ask your IB coordinator for predicted grades early — most Japanese applications are decided on predictions, an essay, a transcript and references.
Check whether each programme wants SAT/ACT or the EJU on top of the IB. If it does, book the test by autumn 2026.
Submit direct to each university through its own online portal, paying a separate application fee each time.
If you want a MEXT scholarship, apply separately through the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen — it is a different process on a different timetable from the university application.
Once you hold an offer, the university applies for your Certificate of Eligibility. You then take that to the Japanese embassy for the student visa. Allow three months.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is document-based and often interview-based rather than exam-based for English-taught programmes: transcript, predicted grades, personal statement, references and sometimes an online interview. This suits IB students who write well. The competitive bar at Kyoto, Waseda's Political Science and Economics, and Keio is high; APU, Akita and several regional programmes are more accessible.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Limited but real — roughly forty fully English-taught bachelor's degrees nationally, concentrated at Waseda (six schools), Keio, Sophia, ICU, Tohoku, Kyushu, Tsukuba, APU and Akita. The single largest programme, UTokyo PEAK, has closed.
language.englishProof: IB English A or B is normally accepted. Where a test is required the usual bars are IELTS or TOEFL iBT, but specific scores were not verified from official pages in this research.
notes: Kyoto iUP explicitly states that Japanese proficiency is not required at the outset — the six-month preparatory course exists to build it.
No English-taught programme requires Japanese to enrol, but essentially all of them require you to study it, and you will need it for part-time work, housing and daily life.
APU and ICU are formally bilingual: you take courses in both languages as your Japanese improves.

tuitionEuEea.value: Japan charges the same tuition to all nationalities — there is no EU/non-EU split. See tuitionNonEu.

notes: We could not read a single official Japanese tuition table during this research — the relevant pages are PDFs or JavaScript-rendered and did not return content. Every figure is therefore left blank here rather than guessed at.

The structure to expect: national universities charge a one-off admission fee plus an annual tuition fee, both set nationally. Private universities (Waseda, Keio, Sophia, ICU, APU) charge considerably more and vary by faculty, with science and engineering highest.
Budget separately for the admission fee, which is charged once and is substantial, and for compulsory facility or lab fees at private universities.
Tokyo living costs are high; Beppu (APU), Akita and Sendai (Tohoku) are dramatically cheaper.

funding: MEXT (Monbukagakusho) Undergraduate Scholarship — the Japanese government scholarship, applied for through the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen roughly a year before entry. It covers tuition, pays a monthly stipend and includes airfare, and normally includes a preparatory Japanese-language year. Amounts were not verified in this research.
University-recommendation MEXT places — some universities nominate their own admitted students. Ask each admissions office whether it holds MEXT quota places.
JASSO Honors Scholarship — a monthly grant administered by the Japan Student Services Organization for privately financed international students. Amount not verified.

Institutional awards decided at admission: Waseda states that recipients of its scholarships are determined by the admission result with no separate application, and that its awards are grants rather than loans.
APU operates tuition-reduction scholarships awarded at admission at several percentage levels — the levels were not verified.
Kyoto iUP offers admission and tuition fee waivers plus monthly scholarships to eligible students.
Danish SU: studying for a full degree outside the EU/EEA follows different rules from studying inside it. Check su.dk before assuming SU will travel with you.
workRights: Students on a Student residence status may work part-time only after obtaining Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted, normally capped at 28 hours a week during term and longer in official holidays. Not re-verified from an official page in this research — confirm with the Immigration Services Agency.
residency: Non-visa-waiver process regardless of EU citizenship. The university applies for a Certificate of Eligibility on your behalf once you accept an offer; you then take it to the Embassy of Japan in Copenhagen for a Student visa. On arrival you receive a residence card and must register at the local municipal office within 14 days and enrol in National Health Insurance.
housing: Most English-taught programmes guarantee or strongly prioritise first-year places in a university dormitory or international house, which is by far the easiest route and usually cheaper than the private market. APU houses all first-year international students in AP House. Private renting in Japan involves key money, guarantor requirements and agency fees that are difficult to navigate from abroad — take the dormitory.
healthcare: Enrolment in Japan's National Health Insurance is compulsory for anyone staying more than three months and is arranged at the municipal office when you register. It covers roughly 70% of medical costs; students typically add the university's own supplementary cover. Your Danish EHIC does not apply in Japan.

institutions.name: University of Tokyo
institutions.englishBachelors: None for 2027 entry. PEAK, the liberal-arts English programme at Komaba, states that September 2026 was its final intake. The Global Science Course is a third-year transfer route requiring two years of prior university study abroad.
institutions.note: Japan's most prestigious university, and as of 2027 entry effectively closed to English-speaking school-leavers. Worth planning towards as a master's destination instead.

institutions.name: Kyoto University
institutions.englishBachelors: iUP — a 4.5-year route: six months of intensive preparatory Japanese, then four years of undergraduate study across a range of faculties. No Japanese required at the start.
institutions.note: The most interesting Japanese option for an IB student in 2027: guidelines for October 2027 enrolment were published in July 2026, and fee waivers plus monthly scholarships are on offer. Kyoto has more Nobel laureates than any other Asian university.

institutions.name: Waseda University
institutions.englishBachelors: Six schools: Political Science and Economics, Social Sciences, International Liberal Studies (SILS), Culture Media and Society, Fundamental Science and Engineering, Creative Science and Engineering. SILS and Culture Media and Society also take April entrants.
institutions.note: The widest English-taught choice in Japan by a distance, under one application window that ran 8 January to 10 February in the last cycle — late enough to use settled predicted grades. Scholarships are decided from the admission result with no separate application.

institutions.name: Keio University
institutions.englishBachelors: PEARL (Programme in Economics for Alliances, Research and Leadership) in the Faculty of Economics, and GIGA (Global Information and Governance Academic) in Environment and Information Studies at Shonan Fujisawa. Details not verified from an official page in this research.
institutions.note: Japan's oldest private university and Waseda's historic rival, with the strongest corporate alumni network in the country. PEARL is a genuine English-medium economics degree; GIGA is a technology-and-policy hybrid on the Shonan Fujisawa campus.

institutions.name: Sophia University
institutions.englishBachelors: Faculty of Liberal Arts (FLA), plus English-taught science and engineering and Sustainable Development programmes. Programme list not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: A Jesuit university in central Tokyo whose Faculty of Liberal Arts has taught entirely in English since the 1940s — the longest-running English-medium undergraduate faculty in Japan. Small, central and internationally minded.

institutions.name: Tohoku University
institutions.englishBachelors: Future Global Leadership (FGL) — three English-taught undergraduate courses: Advanced Molecular Chemistry, Applied Marine Biology, and International Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. Details not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: The strongest English-taught science and engineering option at a Japanese national university, in Sendai — a comfortable, affordable city far cheaper than Tokyo. FGL is small and specialised: three courses, not a faculty.

institutions.name: International Christian University
institutions.englishBachelors: A single bilingual Bachelor of Arts in Liberal Arts with 31 majors; you declare your major at the end of second year. Entry is possible in April or September.
institutions.note: The closest thing Japan has to a small American liberal-arts college: one degree, 31 majors, taught bilingually, on a wooded campus in western Tokyo. The declare-late structure is unusually forgiving for an IB student who is not yet sure.

institutions.name: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University
institutions.englishBachelors: Three colleges, all offering fully English-taught degrees: Asia Pacific Studies (APS), International Management (APM, AACSB-accredited) and Sustainability and Tourism (ST). April and September intakes.
institutions.note: About half the student body is international, from ninety-odd countries — the most genuinely multinational campus in Japan. Beppu is a hot-spring town on Kyushu, which makes it cheap and beautiful but remote. Tuition-reduction scholarships are awarded at admission.

institutions.name: Akita International University
institutions.englishBachelors: All teaching is in English. Bachelor of Arts in Global Business, Global Studies, or Japan Studies (Global Connectivity). A year abroad is compulsory for every student.
institutions.note: A tiny public university in northern Japan where every class is in English and every student must spend a year at a partner university abroad. Famous in Japan for its 24-hour library and for graduate employment rates that embarrass far larger institutions.

institutions.name: Kyushu University
institutions.englishBachelors: International Undergraduate Programmes in Engineering and in Bioresource and Bioenvironment, taught in English. Not verified from an official page in this research.
institutions.note: A large national university in Fukuoka, the most liveable big city in Japan and the closest to the Asian mainland. Its English engineering track is one of the few at a national university outside Tohoku.

institutions.name: University of Tsukuba
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor's Programme in Global Issues (BPGI) and the Interdisciplinary Global Studies track, both taught in English. Not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: Japan's purpose-built science city, an hour north of Tokyo, with the highest concentration of research institutes in the country. Strong in sport science — it trains a large share of Japan's Olympic coaches.

institutions.name: Temple University, Japan Campus
institutions.englishBachelors: All undergraduate degrees are taught in English — it is an American university operating in Tokyo, awarding a US Temple University degree.
institutions.note: The oldest and largest foreign university campus in Japan, on a purpose-built site in Sangenjaya. Useful if you want an American-style degree and the option to transfer to Philadelphia, but it charges American tuition.

institutions.name: Hokkaido University
institutions.englishBachelors: Integrated Science Program (ISP) in the Modern Japanese Studies and science faculties, taught in English. Not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: Founded on an American land-grant model and still the leading Japanese university for agriculture, fisheries and cold-region science. Sapporo is spacious and snowy, and the campus is the most beautiful in Japan.

institutions.name: Nagoya University
institutions.englishBachelors: The G30 International Programs — English-taught bachelor's degrees in Automotive Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Biological Science, Economics and Japan-in-Asia Cultural Studies. Not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: Nagoya's G30 programme is one of the broadest English-taught offerings at a Japanese national university, and it sits in the middle of Japan's car industry — Toyota's home region. Six Nobel laureates in the sciences since 2000.

institutions.name: Osaka University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught undergraduate tracks in the School of Human Sciences and in chemistry/biology. Not verified from an official page.
institutions.note: One of Japan's strongest research universities, particularly in immunology and robotics, in a city with a reputation for being blunter and friendlier than Tokyo. English-taught bachelor provision is thin — check carefully before counting on it.
